final_message:
Done. All 4 existing tests pass unmodified.

**`reportgen/config.py`** — the old `DEFAULTS` dict is replaced by a frozen dataclass whose field defaults are the former dict values:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Config:
    title: str = "Report"
    output_format: str = "text"  # "text" or "markdown"
    max_rows: int = 10
    include_summary: bool = True
```

`load_config` validates the JSON keys against `fields(Config)` before constructing, so an unrecognized key raises `ValueError: unknown config setting: 'colour'` naming the offender. Known keys still override defaults; missing ones fall back.

**`reportgen/formatter.py`, `reportgen/loader.py`** — mechanical switch to attribute access (`config.title`, `config.output_format`, `config.include_summary`, `config.max_rows`). `main.py` and `__init__.py` needed no change since they only pass the object through. A grep for `cfg[`/`config[` across `reportgen/` comes back empty.

Two notes on judgment calls:

- I validate keys explicitly rather than letting `Config(**raw)` fail on its own. `TypeError` from an unexpected kwarg would technically catch the same cases, but the requirement specifies `ValueError`, and the explicit check reports the bad key on its own terms rather than through a constructor message.
- Validation is name-only, matching the old behavior for everything else. A JSON file with `{"max_rows": "ten"}` still builds a `Config` with a string there and fails later at the slice, exactly as the dict version did — dataclasses don't enforce annotations at runtime. Adding type coercion or checking would be a behavior change beyond the stated scope; say the word if you'd like it, `__post_init__` is the natural place.

Working tree has only the three modified files — no commits, no changes under `tests/`, and I removed the `__pycache__` directories pytest left behind.
